key_insight: Reasoning-enabled LLMs can improve SOC detection triage, but they need a separate confidence calibrator because chain-of-thought hurts direct label confidence.
engineering_relevance: For security operations, this means automation can be safer and more effective when models both reason about threats and estimate verdict reliability before triage decisions.
method: Train a chain-of-thought triage classifier on human-labeled Windows endpoint detections.
Use automated prompt optimization, self-training, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
Add a separate calibrator that reads the full reasoning trace to predict whether the verdict is correct.
evidence_signal: On real Windows endpoint detection data, the system reached 82.6% test accuracy and improved high-confidence benign recall by 43.0% and malicious recall by 18.3% over a direct-label classifier.
watch_item: High-confidence automation depends on the trained calibrator; without it, an untrained confidence judge can collapse recall at the operating point used for triage.
paper_title: Cybersecurity Detection Classification with Reasoning-enabled Language Models
